blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The crust is the outermost surface layer of the Earth that supports life.
Continental crust is thicker (avg. 35 km) compared to oceanic crust (5–10 km).
Continental crust is predominantly composed of granite, while oceanic crust consists mainly of basalt.
Oxygen (46%) and Silicon (28%) constitute the vast majority of the crust's elemental composition, alongside Aluminum and Iron.

blocks.content: • Continental crust is composed mainly of granite.

items: Rock Types: Continental crust is granitic, whereas oceanic crust is basaltic.
Elemental Composition: Oxygen (46%) is the most abundant element in the crust, followed by Silicon (28%).
Thickness Difference: Oceanic crust is significantly thinner (5–10 km) than continental crust (35 km).

blocks.content: • Oceanic crust is composed mainly of basalt.
• Major elements: Oxygen (46%), Silicon (28%), Aluminum, Iron.
